paper.title: Adaptive Crowdsourcing Algorithms for the Bandit Survey Problem

unmapped: Each sample is a categorical observation over n options; goal is to identify the mode (most probable option) of the single crowd's response distribution and stop
learner knows the number of options n
settings.definition_quote: Consider a special case with only one crowd to choose from. ... the algorithm reduces to what we call a single-crowd stopping rule: an online algorithm which in every round inputs an option x and decides whether to stop. A single-crowd stopping rule is characterized by two quantities that are to be minimized: the expected stopping time and the error rate

unmapped: Arms (crowds) yield categorical samples over n options; all crowds share the same unique mode x*, which must be output at a stopping time

objective trades off expected total cost sum_t c_{i_t} against the error rate, compared with omniscient benchmarks (best fixed crowd / best fixed distribution over crowds) run with the same stopping rule
settings.definition_quote: In each round t, the algorithm picks some crowd i=i_t and receives an independent sample from the corresponding response distribution D_i. Eventually the algorithm must stop and output its guess for x^*. Each crowd i has a known per-round cost c_i. The algorithm has two objectives to minimize: the total cost sum_t c_{i_t} and the error rate

algorithms.name: Single-crowd stopping rule (stop if empirical gap * N > C sqrt(N))
AlgUnif (uniform discretization of distributions over crowds + UCB with virtual rewards, doubling phases)

symbols.eps_gap: gap of the crowd: difference between largest and second-largest probabilities of its response distribution

source.label: thm:single-crowd
source.quote: Consider the stopping rule~\refeq{eq:stopping-rule} with $\errorC = \sqrt{\log (\tfrac{n}{\delta}\, \NSamples{i}{t}^2 )}$, for some $\delta>0$. The error rate of this stopping rule is at most $O(\delta)$, and the expected stopping time is at most $O\left( \gap_i^{-2}\, \log \tfrac{n}{\delta \gap_i} \right)$.

source.label: thm:single-crowd
source.quote: The error rate of this stopping rule is at most $O(\delta)$

results.notes: Error rate (probability of outputting a wrong option) at most O(delta); probability field set to expectation as the quantity itself is a probability.

conditions: stopping rule has worst-case error rate less than delta

source.label: thm:single-crowd-LB
source.quote: Let $R_0$ be any single-crowd stopping rule with worst-case error rate less than $\delta$. When applied to a crowd with gap $\gap>0$, the expected stopping time of $R_0$ is at least $\Omega(\gap^{-2} \log \tfrac{1}{\delta})$.

results.notes: Paper says it follows from classical coin-tossing results; no proof given.

symbols.Lambda: sum_{i != i*} (c_i (f_{i*} - f_i))^{-2}, with virtual rewards f_i = gap_i/sqrt(c_i)

conditions: R_0 is a symmetric single-crowd stopping rule
R_0 must stop after at most T rounds
i* = argmin_i c_i/gap_i^2 is the approximate best crowd

source.label: thm:UCB
source.quote: Let $i^* = \argmin_i c_i/\gap^2_i$ be the approximate best crowd. Let $R_0$ be a symmetric single-crowd stopping rule. Assume $R_0$ must stop after at most $T$ rounds. Define \AlgUCB by~\refeq{eq:UCB-index} with $C = \sqrt{8\log t}$... Then $ \cost(\AlgUCB|R_0) \leq \cost(i^*|R_0) + O(\Lambda \log T).$

results.notes: Bound is on the excess expected total cost over the (approximate) deterministic benchmark cost(i*|R0). T is the maximal stopping time of R_0, not a horizon given to the algorithm. Proof sketch only.

symbols.sum_c_mu: sum_i c_i mu_i for the algorithm's sampling distribution mu over crowds

conditions: non-adaptive crowd-selection algorithms (crowd sampled i.i.d. from a fixed distribution mu)
R_0 symmetric with worst-case error rate rho
composite stopping rule does not use the total crowd
eps-simple instances: two options, uniform costs, one crowd with gap eps>0 and all others gap 0

source.label: thm:LB
source.quote: Let $R_0$ be a symmetric single-crowd stopping rule with worst-case error rate $\rho$. Assume that the composite stopping rule does not use the total crowd. Consider a non-adaptive crowd-selection algorithm $\A$ whose distribution over crowds is $\mu$. Then for each $\gap>0$, the competitive ratio over the $\gap$-simple problem instances is at least $ \frac{\sum_i c_i\,\mu_i}{\min_i c_i\,\mu_i}\; (1-2k\rho)$

results.notes: Minimizing over mu gives k(1-2k rho), attained by randomized round-robin.

symbols.f_star: maximal induced gap over distributions mu over crowds

conditions: uniform costs
R_0 is the total-crowd stopping rule: stop iff empirical gap of total crowd > C/sqrt(t) or t = T

source.label: thm:AlgUnif
source.quote: Consider the \problem with uniform costs. Let $R_0$ be the single-crowd stopping rule given by~\refeq{eq:stopping-rule-total}. There exists a crowd-selection algorithm $\A$ such that $ \cost(\A|R_0) \leq O\left( (f^*)^{-(k+2)}\; \sqrt{\log T} \right).$

results.notes: Expected total cost (stopping time up to the uniform cost). Proved via reduction Lemma 6.3 (cost O((f*)^{-1/gamma} sqrt(log T)) given MAB regret O(t^{1-gamma} log T) w.p. 1-1/T) and Lipschitz-MAB uniform discretization; the paper notes the algorithm is possibly inefficient. T is the stopping rule's horizon.

conditions: uniform costs
error rate rho > 0 and T >= T(rho)
tuning: R_0 chosen as the stopping rule from the absolute deterministic benchmark

source.label: thm:UCB-bi
source.quote: (a) Deterministic benchmark. There exists a \Algorithm $(\A,R_0)$ such that $\cost(\A|R_0) \leq \bench(i^*,\rho,T) + O(\Lambda \log T)$, where $\Lambda = \sum_{i\neq i^*} (\bias_{i^*}-\bias_i)^{-2}$, $\error(\A|R_0) \leq (k+1)\,\rho.$

results.notes: Excess expected cost over the absolute deterministic benchmark (bi-criteria result, error rate (k+1)rho).

symbols.rho: target worst-case error rate of the benchmark

conditions: uniform costs
T >= T(rho)
results.notes: Worst-case error rate of the combined algorithm, part (a).

symbols.B_rand: absolute randomized benchmark cost bench(mu*, rho, T)

conditions: uniform costs
T >= T(rho)
tuning: quality parameter of total-crowd stopping rule tuned so worst-case error matches the benchmark's

source.label: thm:UCB-bi
source.quote: (b) Randomized benchmark. There exists a \Algorithm $(\A,R_0)$ such that $\cost(\A|R_0) \leq O(\log T \log \tfrac{1}{\rho}) \;(\bench(\mu^*,\rho,T))^{1+k/2}$, $\error(\A|R_0) \leq (k+1)\,\rho.$

results.notes: Comparator is the best fixed distribution over crowds (mapped to best_policy).

conditions: uniform costs
T >= T(rho)

symbols.rho: worst-case error rate of the single-crowd stopping rule R_0

conditions: non-committing crowd-selection algorithm
R_0 symmetric with worst-case error rate rho
composite stopping rule does not use the total crowd

source.label: lm:error-rate-LB
source.quote: Let $R_0$ be a symmetric single-crowd stopping rule with worst-case error rate $\rho$. Let $\A$ be a non-committing crowd-selection algorithm, and let $R$ be the composite stopping rule based on $R_0$ which does not use the total crowd. If $\A$ is used in conjunction with $R$, the worst-case error rate is at least $\rho\,(1-2k\rho)$

results.notes: Lower bound on worst-case error rate of the composite algorithm.
